caption: Figure2: Head-to-head win rate percentages of (row condition) over (column condition) across two datasets, four metrics, and 125 questions per comparison (each repeated five times and averaged). The overall winner per dataset and metric is shown in bold. Self-win rates were not computed but are shown as the expected 50% for reference. All Graph RAG conditions outperformed naïve RAG on comprehensiveness and diversity. Conditions C1-C3 also showed slight improvements in answer comprehensiveness and diversity over TS (global text summarization without a graph index).

Figure3: How the entity references detected in the HotPotQA dataset<ref type="bibr" target="#b68">(Yang et al., 2018)</ref> varies with chunk size and self-reflection iterations for our generic entity extraction prompt with gpt-4-turbo.

Figure4: Graph communities detected using the Leiden algorithm<ref type="bibr" target="#b60">(Traag et al., 2019)</ref> over the MultiHop-RAG (Tang and Yang, 2024) dataset as indexed. Circles represent entity nodes with size proportional to their degree. Node layout was performed via OpenORD<ref type="bibr" target="#b37">(Martin et al., 2011)</ref> and Force Atlas 2<ref type="bibr" target="#b20">(Jacomy et al., 2014)</ref>. Node colors represent entity communities, shown at two levels of hierarchical clustering: (a) Level 0, corresponding to the hierarchical partition with maximum modularity, and (b) Level 1, which reveals internal structure within these root-level communities.
